description: Sequencer running a sixteen-bit linear feedback shift register that can be split into two independently clocked registers, with the bits also read across a four by four grid, superseded by LFSR16 Poly

params.text: Switches one feedback coefficient on or off; the register bits whose coefficient is on are combined to make the bit shifted in
Makes the first register feed back the inverted bit, an XNOR rather than an XOR
Makes the second register feed back the inverted bit, an XNOR rather than an XOR
Sets how many of the sixteen bits belong to the first register, 0 to 16, the rest forming the second register

inputs.text: A rising edge shifts the first register one place, reading high above 2V and low below 0.1V
A rising edge shifts the second register one place, reading high above 2V and low below 0.1V

outputs.text: A voltage built from the four bits of one column of the grid, 0V to 1V, the four bits not being weighted as a plain binary number
The four bits of one row of the grid read as a binary number, 0V to 1V
Carries 10V when the four bits of one column of the grid hold an odd number of set bits, and 0V otherwise
Carries 10V when the four bits of one row of the grid hold an odd number of set bits, and 0V otherwise
Carries 10V while the lowest bit of the first register is set, despite the tooltip naming it sequence 2
Carries 10V while the lowest bit of the second register is set

notes: each square light gives one register bit, red in the first register and green in the second, and brighter where the bit is set
the first register is shifted only by a rising edge at CLK1 and the second only by one at CLK2; with nothing patched there the outputs never change
every feedback coefficient starts switched off, so a register shifts in zeros and falls silent within a few clocks; switch at least one coefficient on for a repeating sequence
the maker marks this module deprecated and points to LFSR16 Poly instead, so it is left out of the module browser unless the browser is set to show deprecated modules
